sheet-2.description: The business centre of Metuchen, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. The sheet covers both sides of Main Street from Middlesex Avenue at the top down to Pennsylvania Avenue and the Pennsylvania Railroad tracks at the bottom, with Pearl Street along the left edge and Robins Place along the right. New Street, Highland Avenue and Hillside Avenue cross the sheet, and Inn Place and Station Place run south from Hillside Avenue toward the railroad. Main Street is lined with two- and three-storey stores in frame and brick, among them two banks (one with a hall on the second and third floors), drug stores, a plumber and a paint store. The post office and the Eagle Fire Co. fire department with its hose tower stand at the corner of Main Street and Pennsylvania Avenue, and the Washington Hose Co. No. 1 fire house and a fifty-car garage face Middlesex Avenue. Other buildings named are the Centenary M.E. Church at Middlesex Avenue and Main Street, the 2nd Baptist Church (colored) on Pearl Street, the League House or Franklin Civic House, a telephone exchange on Hillside Avenue, Edgar Clay's building with an office and chemical laboratory on Station Place, G. Costa's ice and ice cream factory with cold storage, a bakery, a fireproof flour and feed warehouse beside the tracks, auto repair shops and a dry cleaner. Dwellings fill the blocks away from Main Street. Water pipes with their sizes are drawn along the streets, and the P.R.R. passenger depot appears at the bottom edge.
notes: Pilot sheet of the atlas; scale bar printed in feet (Scale of Feet) at the bottom left.
The P.R.R. here is today's Northeast Corridor.
50 ft to an inch. Downtown: Main St, Middlesex Av, Pearl St, New St, Highland Av, Hillside Av, Inn Pl, Station Pl, Robins Pl, Pennsylvania Av. One part. Pilot sheet (ink 100).

sheet-3.description: A residential part of Metuchen drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with the street grid turned about 34 degrees from the page. Middlesex Avenue crosses the top of the sheet, with Linden Avenue entering it from the north near the top centre. Highland Avenue runs across the middle, from Robins Place on the left to Rector Street on the right, and Washington Place branches from Robins Place toward Pleasant. Hillside Avenue closes the sheet along the bottom. The long blocks between Middlesex and Highland avenues are lined with single-family dwellings in frame, many with tile or fireproof roofs shown in pink, and with small outbuildings and garages in the rear. A Masonic Building stands on the left at Middlesex Avenue and a small brick-roofed building at the top right corner. The blocks south of Highland Avenue are numbered 118 to 120 and also hold dwellings, with a compass rose in the large block at lower left. Six-inch water pipes are marked along Middlesex, Highland and Hillside avenues, and street widths of 50 feet are noted. The neighbouring sheets are numbered in the margins: 14 and 15 at the top, 2 at left and 16 below. There are no industrial buildings or railroads on this sheet.
notes: Robins Place, Pleasant and Rector appear as 'Pleasant Place' and 'Rector Street' in OpenStreetMap.
Fitted rotation about 34 degrees, 7.95 px/ft; the control points all lie in the lower half of the sheet.
50 ft. One part. Middlesex Av, Linden Av, Highland Av, Washington Pl, Robins Pl, Pleasant, Hillside Av, Rector; Masonic Building. Control all in the lower half.

sheet-4.description: The western edge of Metuchen's centre, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the grid turned only a few degrees. Main Street runs down the right-hand edge and Amboy Avenue crosses the lower part of the sheet from Main Street to the left margin. Graham Avenue and Thomas enter Amboy Avenue from the north and south respectively. The upper left is crossed by the main lines of the Pennsylvania Railroad, with a freight station, platforms and a signal tower beside the tracks, and the upper right is occupied by a cemetery. Between the railroad and Amboy Avenue lie dwelling blocks numbered 144 and 145 along Thomas and Main, mostly small frame houses with some in tile. South of Amboy Avenue the Lehigh Valley Railroad crosses the sheet diagonally at the lower left, and The Reformed Church with its Sunday school and a small group of houses and an auto repair shop face Amboy Avenue near Graham Avenue. A wooden bridge is noted at the bottom, where Graham Avenue crosses the Lehigh Valley line. Water pipes of 6 and 12 inches are drawn in Main Street and Amboy Avenue. Neighbouring sheets 2, 5, 6, 7, 9 and 11 are noted in the margins.
notes: Thomas is today's Halsey Street (Amboy Avenue / Halsey Street).
The Lehigh Valley railroad shown here is gone; its line is now the Middlesex Greenway Trail.
Placed from three points all on Amboy Avenue (one hand-picked): low confidence.

50 ft. One part. Amboy Av, Main, Thomas (today Halsey Street), Graham Av; P.R.R. main lines and freight station, L.V.R.R., cemetery, Reformed Church. Placed from three points on Amboy Avenue (helmert, low confidence).

sheet-5.description: Blocks east of Main Street in the centre of Metuchen, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the grid turned about 6 degrees. Main Street forms the left side of the sheet and Woodbridge Avenue crosses the top; Henry and Home streets run down the right half and Amboy Avenue closes the bottom. Clinton Place and Bissett Place cut across between Main and Henry. The upper left corner shows the Pennsylvania Railroad tracks with the passenger station, and above Woodbridge Avenue stands the Presbyterian Church. The 1st Baptist Church stands on Clinton Place. The Forum Theatre, a large brick building with lobby and stage, fronts Main Street on Bissett Place. Elsewhere the blocks hold two-storey frame dwellings with small garages, and long narrow lots drawn along the south side of Bissett Place. The blocks are numbered 164, 182, 183, 183A and 183B. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 12 inches are shown, and a scale of feet at the bottom.
notes: Henry is today's Carlton Road; Home is Home Street.
Fitted 7.97 px/ft, rotation -5.6 degrees, 9 points.
50 ft. One part. Main, Woodbridge Av, Clinton Pl, Bissett Pl, Henry (today Carlton Road), Home, Amboy Av; passenger station, Presbyterian and 1st Baptist churches, Forum Theatre.

sheet-6.description: The southern end of Metuchen's centre, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Main Street runs down the right-hand edge and Graham Avenue runs down the centre-right. Spring street crosses the upper third, Franklyn Place the middle and High the bottom, with a stub of Thomas St. below High at the lower left. The top is crossed by railroad lines, the Pennsylvania Railroad and the Lehigh Valley, with a wooden bridge drawn where Graham Avenue and Main Street pass over them. Blocks 147, 149, 150 and 151 are filled with small frame dwellings with some larger lots, and a hardware and paints store with a plaster shed stands on Main Street at the lower right. A compass rose with a north arrow is placed in the open ground at left centre. Six-inch water pipes lie along Spring, High and Main. Neighbouring sheets 4, 7, 9 and 18 are noted at the edges.
notes: Franklyn Place is today's Franklin Place.
Control: 4 points; Main / High and Thomas / High were not detected.
50 ft. One part. Spring, Graham Av, Main, Franklyn Pl, High, Thomas St; P.R.R. on wooden bridges. Four points.

sheet-7.description: The southeastern part of the town centre of Metuchen, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Amboy Avenue runs across the top with Henry and Home streets entering it from the north; Main Street runs down the left side and Lincoln Avenue closes the bottom, with George Street at the lower right. Tulsa Avenue crosses the middle, joined by Howell. The Lehigh Valley Railroad crosses the sheet diagonally from the left to the lower right, with a wooden bridge where Main Street crosses it, and Spring St. is lettered at the left edge. North of the railroad the long lots on Amboy Avenue hold dwellings and a compass rose sits mid-block. South of the tracks are blocks numbered 208 with dwellings and small garages, and a cemetery appears at the right. Water pipes of 6 and 12 inches are drawn along Amboy Avenue, Main and Lincoln Avenue. Neighbouring sheets are 4, 5, 6, 16 and 19.
notes: Henry is today's Carlton Road; Home is Home Street; Spring Street is today's Spring Street.
Fitted scale is 2 percent above the 50 ft constant; Spring Street left out of the fit (3.1 m residual).
50 ft. One part. Amboy Av, Henry St, Home St, Main, Spring St, Tulsa Av, Howell, Lincoln Av, George St; L.V.R.R., cemetery. Spring Street left out (3.1 m).

sheet-8-1.description: The south-west edge of Metuchen at 100 feet to an inch, north roughly up. Amboy Avenue crosses the top of the sheet; Bridge Street runs down the left side past Cornell Avenue and Connor Avenue, both marked not opened, and Hampton runs north from Middlesex Avenue. The Pennsylvania Railroad main lines cross the sheet from left to right on an embankment, with wooden bridges carrying them over Bridge Street and over Middlesex Avenue, which passes under the tracks and continues south-west toward the borough line. Essex Avenue branches east from Middlesex Avenue near Bridge Street, Prospect runs south-east from Essex Avenue to High, which crosses the bottom of the sheet, and Kentnor (marked not opened at its north end) runs down the right side. The P.R.R. Bonhamtown Branch curves south across the sheet from the main line, with a steel bridge, a coal trestle and a coal yard beside it, and Gallup Place (not opened) is laid out in small lots east of it. Most of the sheet is open land in large blocks (76 to 78, 128 to 131, 135 to 139, 152 and 153) with scattered frame dwellings, a saw mill with electric motor, an auto repair shop and a filling station on Middlesex Avenue, coops, a dairy on High Street and an office. A walled-off area at the upper right is a separate inset of Middlesex Avenue at the borough line.
notes: Middlesex Avenue south-west of the railroad is today the Lincoln Highway (NJ 27); the modern Middlesex Avenue meets Bridge Street north of the tracks, a junction not drawn on the sheet, which was left out.
The Hampton Street / New Durham Road junction lay 10 m from the fit and was left out; Amboy Avenue at the top of the sheet may not follow today's New Durham Road.
The P.R.R. Bonhamtown Branch is today the Bonhamtown Industrial Track; the main lines are the Northeast Corridor.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main map (Amboy Av, Bridge, Connor Av, Middlesex Av, Essex Av, Prospect, High, Kentnor, P.R.R. main lines and Bonhamtown Branch); 2 inset (top right, heavy line) of Middlesex Av (today Lincoln Highway) at the western borough line, State Police headquarters, placed from one point at the borough line.

sheet-8-2.description: An inset at the upper right of sheet 8, walled off by a heavy line and drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow, showing Middlesex Avenue (a 66-foot street) where it leaves the borough. The dash-dot borough line runs down the left side of the inset and crosses Middlesex Avenue at lot 952. North of the avenue is block 127 with a few frame dwellings and outbuildings and the State Police headquarters; south of it is part of block 130 with a dwelling, a coop and other small outbuildings, and the corner of the inset holds the edge of the railroad embankment. House numbers 928 to 952 are printed along Middlesex Avenue.
notes: Middlesex Avenue here is today the Lincoln Highway (NJ 27).

Placed from one hand-picked point, the borough line on the centre of Middlesex Avenue, taken from where the parcel municipality code changes from Metuchen to Edison along the Lincoln Highway, with the sheet scale and north from the printed arrow and the line of the avenue; low confidence.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main map (Amboy Av, Bridge, Connor Av, Middlesex Av, Essex Av, Prospect, High, Kentnor, P.R.R. main lines and Bonhamtown Branch); 2 inset (top right, heavy line) of Middlesex Av (today Lincoln Highway) at the western borough line, State Police headquarters, placed from one point at the borough line.

sheet-9.description: The west end of Metuchen near the Pennsylvania Railroad, drawn at 100 feet to an inch (printed scale). The main line of the railroad and the Lehigh Valley line cross the upper part of the sheet diagonally, with the Amboy Avenue passenger station near the upper right. Essex Avenue crosses the upper third and Spring, High and the streets Rose, Sylvan Avenue, Lake Avenue and Sumitt Avenue cross it. At the left, long narrow building lots are laid out along Kentnor and Newman streets, with a Gallup Place marked not opened, and Nolcini Place cuts into the lots above Essex Avenue. Central Avenue and Holly Street enter at the top right. A park lies beside the railroad with Parkway along it. The blocks are numbered 132 to 134, 140 to 143, 146 to 150 and 153 to 154; most buildings are small frame dwellings with a few tile ones, and there is a filling station at the right. Neighbouring sheets 8, 10, 11, 4, 6 and 18 are named at the edges.
notes: Parkway is today's Memorial Parkway; Sumitt Avenue is Summit Avenue; Sylvan Avenue north of Spring is Cliffwood Place.
100 ft sheet: 4.02 px/ft.

100 ft. One part. Central Av, Holly St, Amboy Av, Parkway (today Memorial Parkway), Nolcini Pl, Essex Av, Gallup Pl, Kentnor, Newman, Rose, Spring, Lake Av, Sylvan Av, Franklyn Pl, Ely Ct, High, Sumitt Av; P.R.R. and L.V.R.R., Amboy Av passenger station, park.

sheet-10-1.description: The western part of Metuchen at 100 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. Durham Avenue crosses the top of the sheet, and a grid of newly platted streets runs south-west from it: Bloomfield Drive, Finch, Electric, Thomas Houston and Edison north of Durham Avenue, and John, Smith and Hampton south of it, crossed by John McManus Avenue. Amboy Avenue runs diagonally across the middle of the sheet, with Volkmar Place, Oliver, Adams and Factory leaving it toward Middlesex Avenue, which crosses the bottom of the sheet above the Pennsylvania Railroad main lines and Essex Avenue. The Lehigh Valley Railroad tracks, with a freight station, a station and a platform, run down the right edge. Most blocks are divided into narrow lots, many streets are marked not opened, and dwellings are scattered, several marked from plans. The largest building is the Empire Floor & Wall Tile Co. factory between Factory Street and the Lehigh Valley tracks, a fireproof saw-tooth roofed building with kilns, a shavings warehouse and an office. Other works are the Public Service Corp. transformer station on Durham Avenue by the railroad, the Metuchen Tile Co. floor tile plant on Middlesex Avenue, and Manning Freeman & Son building supplies, with lumber sheds and a warehouse, near the steel bridge where Middlesex Avenue passes the Lehigh Valley line. A walled-off area at the lower left is a separate inset of Durham Avenue further west.
notes: Amboy Avenue is today New Durham Road; Thomas Houston is today Houston Street; Volkmar Place, Oliver, Adams, Factory, John, Smith and Hampton keep their names as streets (OpenStreetMap).
John McManus Avenue was left out of the control: its junctions lay 6 m from the fit, and its modern equivalent (perhaps McAdams Avenue) was not confirmed.
The Lehigh Valley Railroad line is today the Middlesex Greenway Trail.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main map (Durham Av, Bloomfield Drive, Finch, Electric, Thomas Houston, Edison, John, McManus Av, Smith, Hampton, Amboy Av = New Durham Road, Volkmar Pl, Oliver, Adams, Factory, Middlesex Av; Empire Floor & Wall Tile Co, Lehigh Valley RR); 2 inset (lower left, heavy line) of Durham Av at Weston and Westinghouse, Metuchen Dyestuff Corp ruins.

sheet-10-2.description: An inset at the lower left of sheet 10, walled off by a heavy line and drawn at 100 feet to an inch, showing Durham Avenue west of the main map where Weston and Westinghouse meet it from the north. Block 39 (old number 99) between Weston and Westinghouse is divided into narrow lots with a single two-storey dwelling; block 38 lies to the north-west. South of Durham Avenue, in block 61 (old 106), are the ruins of the Metuchen Dyestuff Corp. works after a fire, with a tile outbuilding, and a dwelling and shed near the road. Six-inch water pipes are drawn in Durham Avenue with a hydrant.
notes: Weston and Westinghouse are today Weston Street and Westinghouse Street.

Placed from two detected junctions about 70 m apart (a helmert); its rotation (27 degrees) agrees with the main part of the sheet, not with the inset's own north arrow, which points nearly straight up; low confidence.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main map (Durham Av, Bloomfield Drive, Finch, Electric, Thomas Houston, Edison, John, McManus Av, Smith, Hampton, Amboy Av = New Durham Road, Volkmar Pl, Oliver, Adams, Factory, Middlesex Av; Empire Floor & Wall Tile Co, Lehigh Valley RR); 2 inset (lower left, heavy line) of Durham Av at Weston and Westinghouse, Metuchen Dyestuff Corp ruins.

sheet-11.description: The northern part of Metuchen's central district at 100 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. The sheet runs from Maple Avenue at the top to New Street and the Pennsylvania Railroad (P.R.R.) at the bottom, and from the Lehigh Valley (L.V.) main line at the left to Pearl Street at the right. Central Avenue crosses the sheet from top to bottom, with Durham Avenue and School crossing it diagonally. Between Central Avenue and Center the blocks along Durham Avenue and School are closely built with one- and two-storey frame dwellings, with a few tile works, a Second Baptist Church, an experimental machine shop (electric motors) and Bethel A.M.E. Church on the west side of Central Avenue. Martin and the blocks above Durham Avenue are long, narrow lots that are mostly vacant. Metuchen High School stands in the middle of the sheet near Center, with an annex to its side. Middlesex Avenue runs across the lower part from the Lehigh Valley bridge at the left to Pearl Street, with a filling station at the corner of Holly, and a private garage near the bottom edge. Campbell Place forms the western block at Central Avenue. At the left edge the sheet shows an Edward W. Lawler second-hand machinery dealer, a cement block factory and the parallel tracks of the Lehigh Valley and the P.R.R. Block numbers 54 to 115, with old numbers in brackets, are printed in the blocks. Water pipes are drawn in most streets.
notes: Holly is today Lake Avenue (OpenStreetMap); Lake Avenue is also lettered at the bottom edge.
Sampson and Campbell Place are not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Sampson was not used as control: the modern Sampson Street line does not follow the street drawn on this sheet.
The New Street / Pearl Street junction lay 24 m from the fit and was rejected.
100 ft. One part. Central Av, Durham Av, Middlesex Av, Center, Martin, Maple Av, Talmadge Av, School, William, Pearl, New, Holly (today Lake Avenue), Sampson, Campbell Pl; Metuchen High School.

sheet-12-1.description: The northern edge of Metuchen at 100 feet to an inch, between the borough line with Raritan Township along the top of the sheet and the Port Reading Railroad (lettered P.R.R.) near the bottom. Plainfield Avenue runs north across the sheet from the railroad crossing, with Central Avenue continuing it south of the tracks, and Olive Street runs along the right edge. West of Plainfield Avenue are the grounds of St. Joseph's College, heated by steam and lit by electricity: a chapel and a three-storey main building, a hose house with a 480-foot six-inch water pipe to a hydrant on Plainfield Avenue, a concrete-filled shed, a two-storey storage building, a garage and a hen coop. East of Plainfield Avenue the large tract numbered 3 is almost wholly open, with scattered dwellings and outbuildings along the avenue and a group of hen coops and a tile coop in the middle, and a few more dwellings toward Olive Street. Street widths of 60 and 66 feet are marked, and a 12-inch water pipe is drawn in Plainfield Avenue and Central Avenue. The lower part of the sheet is cut off by a heavy line below which the sheet carries three insets of outlying works.
notes: Plainfield Avenue north of the railroad is today Plainfield Road; Olive is today Clive Street (OpenStreetMap).
P.R.R. here is the Port Reading Railroad (today the Port Reading Secondary), as named on the key map.
The borough line with Raritan Township (today Edison) is drawn along the top.

100 ft. Four parts: 1 St. Joseph's College, Plainfield Av (today Plainfield Road) and Olive (today Clive Street) north of the Port Reading RR, placed from the two rail crossings (helmert); 2 inset General Ceramics Co porcelain works on Jackson Av (Edison), about 1.5 miles E of P.O., anchored on Jackson Av at the former Lehigh Valley line (Middlesex Greenway); 3 inset Menlo Park, Lincoln Highway, B.H. Lage Inc floor tile, anchored on Evergreen Road / Lincoln Highway; 4 inset Manufactured Rubber Co and Lorraine Oil Co, anchored on the Whitman Av crossing of the Bonhamtown branch. Inset north arrows disagree with the streets by up to 22 degrees on part 3.

sheet-12-2.description: An inset at the lower left of sheet 12, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left, showing the General Ceramics Company porcelain works, located about one and a half miles east of the post office. The works lie along the east side of Jackson Avenue, a 50-foot street drawn down the left edge of the inset, south of the tracks of the Lehigh Valley Railroad (L.V.R.R.) across the top, where a loading platform runs along a siding. The plant is a long group of fireproof and brick buildings: tile packing and shipping, clay storage, an office, kilns, slipping, pressing and drying rooms, a tile wall, a repairing shop, clay mixing and clay bins, an engine room and a chemical room. A trestle about ten feet high curves in from the railroad along the east side of the works. Notes record power and heat by steam, electric lights, a watchman and clock, a chemical cart and fire pails. The rest of the inset is open ground.
notes: Placed from one hand-picked point, Jackson Avenue at the former Lehigh Valley Railroad line (today the Middlesex Greenway Trail), with the scale of the sheet and north from the line of Jackson Avenue; low confidence.
The Jackson Avenue identified is the one in Edison crossing the Middlesex Greenway about 1.8 km east of the Metuchen post office.

100 ft. Four parts: 1 St. Joseph's College, Plainfield Av (today Plainfield Road) and Olive (today Clive Street) north of the Port Reading RR, placed from the two rail crossings (helmert); 2 inset General Ceramics Co porcelain works on Jackson Av (Edison), about 1.5 miles E of P.O., anchored on Jackson Av at the former Lehigh Valley line (Middlesex Greenway); 3 inset Menlo Park, Lincoln Highway, B.H. Lage Inc floor tile, anchored on Evergreen Road / Lincoln Highway; 4 inset Manufactured Rubber Co and Lorraine Oil Co, anchored on the Whitman Av crossing of the Bonhamtown branch. Inset north arrows disagree with the streets by up to 22 degrees on part 3.

sheet-12-3.description: An inset in the middle right of sheet 12, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, headed Menlo Park and noted as located about two miles north-east of the post office. The Lincoln Highway runs across the inset with numbered lots 501 to 544 along both sides; a Road drawn at the left end meets it from the south and passes under the Pennsylvania Railroad (P.R.R.) main line, which runs below the highway with four tracks. Block 301 lies north of the highway with one dwelling, and block 302 between the highway and the railroad holds scattered dwellings, sheds, a saw mill with electric power and, at the east end, the B. H. Lage Inc. floor tile manufacturing plant with mixing and pressing rooms, a kiln room and packing. Notes record steam power and heat, electric lights, hydrants and hose, and a tank on the roof supplied from an artesian well. The north arrow on the inset points about twenty degrees clockwise of up, while the streets place north about forty degrees clockwise.
notes: The Road is identified as today's Evergreen Road, from the distance between the Lincoln Highway and the railroad (about 68 m at the Road, closing toward the east as drawn); placed from that junction and the Evergreen Road railroad crossing; low confidence.
The printed north arrow (about 17 degrees) disagrees with the streets (about 40 degrees); the placement follows the streets.

100 ft. sheet-12-4.description: An inset at the lower right of sheet 12, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the right, showing two works on the Pennsylvania Railroad's Bonhampton Branch. The branch crosses the inset from lower left to upper right and crosses Whitman, a 60-foot street drawn down the right side, where the dash-dot Raritan Township line also crosses. South-west of the crossing stands the Manufactured Rubber Co., makers of reclaimed rubber, with acid, wash, dry and drying houses, stock buildings, a 20,000 gallon reservoir and a sixty-foot frame tank; notes record electric power and lights, steam heat, automatic sprinklers, a watchman and clock, and pumping from an artesian well. Beyond Whitman lies the Lorraine Oil Co. plant, with an oil storage building, a pump, gasoline and oil tanks and an office. The scale bar of the sheet is printed at the bottom of this inset.
notes: Whitman is today Whitman Avenue (Edison); the branch is the Bonhamtown Industrial Track.

Placed from one hand-picked point, the Whitman Avenue railroad crossing, with north from the railroad line (86 degrees) and the sheet scale; the modern road bends at the crossing, so the point may be several metres off; low confidence.

sheet-13-1.description: The north-west quarter of Metuchen at 100 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. The sheet runs from the Port Reading Railroad (P.R.R.) and the Plainfield Avenue crossing at the top left down to Maple Avenue at the bottom, and from Norcross Avenue and the blocks of Forrest Street, Alvin, Liberty Street, Leonard and Pershing at the left to Main Street and Olive at the right. Central Avenue crosses the sheet from the railroad to the bottom, and Plainfield Road runs east from it to the junction with Olive, Christol Street and Main Street. Between them lies a newly laid-out residential district of small, regular lots: Princeton, Rutgers and Midland Avenue cross University Avenue, Harvard Avenue and Columbia Avenue, with Lafayette Avenue (marked not opened) and Center Street further south and Chestnut Avenue below. The blocks east of Central Avenue are closely built with one- and two-storey frame dwellings, some marked as from plans, while the lots west of Norcross Avenue and along Forrest Street are largely vacant. Block 44 near the railroad holds hen houses and tile outbuildings, and a filling station stands on Central Avenue below the crossing. Water pipes of 6 and 12 inches are drawn in most streets with hydrants marked. Harrel Place leaves Main Street at the right edge. Block numbers 44 to 58 (with old numbers in brackets on some) are printed in the blocks. A strip along the top of the sheet, cut off by a heavy line, shows Christol Street east of Main Street and is a separate part.
notes: Olive is today Clive Street; Chestnut Avenue is today West Chestnut Avenue (OpenStreetMap).
Plainfield Avenue north of the railroad is today Plainfield Road; the Plainfield Road of the sheet is today Plainfield Avenue.
Lafayette Avenue is marked not opened.

The University Avenue junctions at Princeton and Rutgers lie 14 to 18 m from the fit to the rest of the sheet and were rejected, which suggests University Avenue north of Midland Avenue has been realigned.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main map (Plainfield Rd = Plainfield Avenue, Central Av, Norcross, Princeton, Rutgers, Midland, University, Harvard, Columbia, Center, Chestnut, Martin, Maple, Main, Olive = Clive Street); 2 strip along the top (heavy line) of Christol St east of Main St to Ross, Home Builders Supply Co (helmert from two points).

sheet-13-2.description: A narrow strip along the top of sheet 13, cut off from the main map by a heavy diagonal line and drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow. It shows Christol Street from its junction with Plainfield Road, Olive and Main Street eastward past Ross, which is marked not opened, with the continuation of Christol east of Ross also marked not opened. North of Christol Street lies block 92 with a row of two-storey frame dwellings and, further east beside the railroad sidings, the Home Builders Supply Co. yard with lumber sheds and scattered lumber. South of Christol lie blocks 93 and 95, mostly vacant, with a single dwelling near Ross. A scale and office stand at the junction with Main Street, and water pipes of 6 and 12 inches are drawn in Christol Street and Plainfield Road.
notes: Placed from two points about 300 m apart (the Christol Street junction with Main Street, hand-picked, and Christol Street / Ross Avenue, detected), so the fit is a helmert; low confidence.
Olive is today Clive Street; Ross is today Ross Avenue; the Plainfield Road of the sheet is today Plainfield Avenue.

100 ft. sheet-14.description: The central district of Metuchen along Main, at 100 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. Main runs from Midland Avenue at the top to its junction with Middlesex Avenue at the bottom, where the old Borough Hall and its police headquarters stand. East of Main the sheet shows the diagonal lines of Chestnut Avenue, Maple Avenue, Elm Avenue and Walnut Place, which run down toward Linden Avenue and Ross at the right edge. These blocks hold closely set dwellings, St. Frances (or St. Stephens) Roman Catholic Church with its parochial school and hall, and a few larger houses on wide lots; the area above Chestnut Avenue and beside Ross is laid out in long, narrow lots that are mostly empty. Harrel Place and Thole are marked as arbitrary lines. West of Main the sheet shows a short Maple Avenue and Talmadge Avenue with small houses on narrow lots, Sampson, William and Durham Avenue, and at the lower left a group of tile and auto repair works along Durham Avenue and Middlesex Avenue, with a filling station beside Main. The large blank area at the upper left is the neighbouring sheet, and holds the compass rose. Block numbers 59 to 104, with old numbers in brackets, are printed in the blocks. Water pipes are drawn in most streets with hydrants marked.
notes: Chestnut Avenue is today East Chestnut Avenue (OpenStreetMap); Ross is today Ross Avenue.
Harrel Place, Thole and Walnut Place are not in the OpenStreetMap extract; Harrel Place and Thole are marked arbitrary on the sheet.
William was not used as control; the modern William Street line sits off the drawn street.
100 ft. One part. Main, Chestnut Av, Maple Av, Elm Av, Walnut Pl, Linden Av, Ross, Middlesex Av, Durham Av, Midland Av, Talmadge Av, William, Thole, Harrel Pl; Borough Hall.

sheet-15.description: A residential strip of south-eastern Metuchen at 100 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. The sheet runs from Linden Avenue and Chestnut Avenue at the top left to Hillside Avenue at the bottom, and from Rector at the left to Grove at the right edge. Middlesex Avenue crosses the sheet diagonally as a wide street of about 80 feet, with Oak Avenue meeting it at an acute fork near the left. North of Middlesex Avenue are lots of one- and two-storey dwellings along Linden Avenue, Maple Avenue and Oak Avenue, a church with its parish house at the lower left corner of that district, and the blocks around Chestnut Avenue, which are mostly open land with a few large houses. South of Middlesex Avenue the blocks between Rector and Huxley Road are built up with small frame houses along Clarendon Court, Beverly Court and Highland Avenue, with larger lots and a few buildings farther down toward Dellwood Road (marked not opened) and Hillside Avenue. A group of bunk houses, an office and a mess room stands on Grove at the lower right. A street east of Grove at the right edge is lettered not named. Block numbers 93 to 125, with old numbers in brackets, are printed in the blocks. A compass rose and the scale bar stand in the blank margin at the left.
notes: Chestnut Avenue is today East Chestnut Avenue (OpenStreetMap); Rector is today Rector Street; Grove is today Grove Avenue.
Dellwood Road is lettered not opened.
The modern Middlesex Avenue / Oak Avenue junction is doubled (two nodes 34 m apart) and only one was used.
Junctions on Grove and Huxley Road carry residuals of 2 to 3 m, and the detector read Grove 100 to 120 ft from where it was first placed.
100 ft. One part. Middlesex Av, Oak Av, Linden Av, Maple Av, Chestnut Av, Clarendon Ct, Beverly Ct, Highland Av, Rector, Huxley Rd, Dellwood Rd, Grove, Hillside Av.

sheet-16.description: The south-eastern part of Metuchen between the Pennsylvania Railroad main line and Amboy Avenue, at 100 feet to an inch. The sheet is turned only slightly, with north near the top. The railroad (P.R.R. main line) crosses the sheet as a band of parallel tracks from the lower left to the upper right, with Pennsylvania Avenue and Hillside Avenue running along its north side and Pleasant crossing between them. South of the tracks, the district from Lauradale and Homer Place across to Blair Avenue is laid out in long, narrow lots, mostly vacant, with a few dwellings along Barnstable, Henry, Wilmer and Stockton and a group of tile works near Blair Avenue. Woodbridge Avenue crosses the sheet from left to right. Below it, the blocks between Home, Bounty, Simpson Place, Voorhees Place, Kempson Place and Peliter Avenue are well built with one- and two-storey frame dwellings, and Washington School stands at the centre of the lower half beside Hunt Place. Hanson Avenue crosses the blocks at the lower right. Amboy Avenue forms the bottom edge, with Green Street, Linsley Place and Coan Place lettered below it as streets that continue on the next sheet. The left third of the sheet is blank land belonging to the neighbouring sheet and holds the compass rose and the scale bar. Block numbers 123 to 188, with old numbers in brackets, are printed in the blocks.
notes: Lauradale, Homer Place, Barnstable, Wilmer, Stockton, Hunt Place and Peliter Avenue are not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
The last street name at the bottom right edge is hard to read and may be Coan Place or Corn Place; it was read as Coan Place from the inset on sheet 19.
The Henry / Jonesdale Avenue junction lay 16 m from the fit and was rejected, so the upper right corner rests on little control.
Pleasant and Pennsylvania Avenue in the upper left are not near any modern street used for control.

100 ft. One part. Pennsylvania RR main line, Woodbridge Av, Home, Bounty, Voorhees Pl, Kempson Pl, Amboy Av, Hillside Av and others; Washington School. Upper right corner has little control (Henry / Jonesdale rejected at 16 m).

sheet-17.description: The eastern edge of Metuchen along the Raritan Township line, at 100 feet to an inch, with the street grid turned a few degrees from the page. Woodbridge Avenue crosses the sheet from left to right and divides two districts. South of it is a regular grid of narrow, deep lots between Peliter Avenue and Sidney Place, cut by Hanson Avenue and ending at Amboy Avenue along the bottom, where short places (Coan, Vail, James, Clifford, Ethel, Goodwill, Pierson) run south from it. The lots from Carson Avenue to Eggert Avenue are the best built, with dwellings and a few tile works; the eastern blocks toward Sidney Place are mostly empty, and a dairy, the ruins of a fire and a row of lettered houses stand at the edge of the open land to the right. The borough line with Raritan Township cuts across the lower right corner. North of Woodbridge Avenue the sheet shows the radial streets Blair Avenue, Grove Avenue and Oakland Avenue converging at the upper left with Henry and Jonesdale Avenue, and, east of them, Upland, Spear, Hollywood Avenue, Hazelwood Avenue and Beechwood Avenue running up from New York Avenue. These blocks are laid out in long, narrow lots and are largely vacant, except for scattered houses on Blair Avenue and Grove Avenue and a large estate with a swimming pool and several outbuildings between Spear and Hazelwood Avenue. Block numbers 172 to 221, with old numbers in brackets, are printed in the blocks. A compass rose stands in the blank left margin.
notes: McCoy Avenue is Mc Coy Avenue in OpenStreetMap; the Hanson Avenue / Mc Coy Avenue junction lay 11.6 m from the fit and was rejected.
Spear, Peliter Avenue, Clifford Place and Pierson Place are not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Amboy Avenue / Coan Place was rejected at 7.5 m and the Hazelwood Avenue / New York Avenue junction at 10.8 m.
The street lettered Grove Avenue meets Henry and Oakland Avenue at a five-way junction that lay 15 m from the fit and was rejected.
100 ft. One part. Woodbridge Av, Hanson Av, Carson, Eggert, McCoy, Sidney Pl, Amboy Av, Grove Av, New York Av, Oakland Av; Raritan Township line.

sheet-18.description: The district west of Main in the south-west of Metuchen, at 100 feet to an inch, with the street grid turned a few degrees from the page. High runs along the top of the sheet, and Main runs down the right edge. At the upper left Sylvan Avenue and the blocks of Park Place, Division and Poplar contain long rows of one- and two-storey dwellings on narrow lots, with a few larger houses on block 154C. Lake Avenue runs through the middle of the sheet, and between it and Thomas the Y.M.C.A. building stands on High with a work shop and poultry sheds behind; the Edgar School (a tile and wall works) stands on Brunswick Avenue. East of Thomas, Walnut and Brunswick Avenue are closely built with small houses, and Sheridan Avenue, Maple Avenue and Cedar carry scattered dwellings marked from plans. The large central area (block 155) is unbuilt land, crossed by the borough line with Raritan Township, and the sheet ends at the bottom with the subdivision of McPherson Avenue, Delta Avenue, Prince and Cortland, whose lots straddle the line. A compass rose and the scale bar are printed in the open land. Blocks 154B to 163, with old numbers in brackets, are marked, and water pipes are drawn in most streets with hydrants marked.
notes: Sumitt Avenue is spelled so on the sheet; the modern street is Summit Avenue.
Walnut is today East Walnut Street or West Walnut Street (OpenStreetMap), and Cedar is today West Cedar Street.
Delta Avenue, Cortland, Prince and Graham Street are not in the OpenStreetMap extract; the McPherson Avenue of the sheet is Mc Pherson Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
The Main Street line of OpenStreetMap lies about 20 m east of the drawn street south of Sheridan Avenue; the Main / Sheridan Avenue junction lay 14.5 m from the fit and was rejected.
The Park Place / Sylvan Avenue junction lay 18 m from the fit and was rejected.

100 ft. One part. High, Lake Av, Thomas, Brunswick Av, Sheridan Av, Sylvan Av, Division, Poplar, Whitman Av, McPherson Av, Delta Av, Main; Raritan Township line. Modern Main Street south of Brunswick Avenue lies 15 to 20 m east of the drawn street.

sheet-19-1.description: The south-western side of Metuchen along Main, at 100 feet to an inch, with the street grid turned a few degrees from the page. Main runs down the left edge of the sheet, with the blocks of the neighbouring sheet showing beyond it, and a row of tile and brick works and stores stands along its east side near Charles. The long east-west streets (Lincoln Avenue, Walnut Avenue, Myrtle Avenue, Orchard Avenue, Maple Avenue and Cedar) cross the sheet from Main and are laid out in long, narrow lots running north and south. The upper part, north of Walnut Avenue, is the best built, with one- and two-storey dwellings along Lincoln Avenue, George, Charles and Laurence; Charles curves between George and its straight stretch toward Laurence, and Lincoln Avenue is lettered not open east of Laurence. The middle and lower blocks are thinly built, with scattered dwellings on Orchard Avenue, Maple Avenue and Cedar, and Christ Adelphian Church stands on a block south of Myrtle Avenue. Block numbers 210 to 218, with old numbers in brackets, are printed in the blocks. A cemetery lies along the upper edge. The lower right of the sheet is cut off by a heavy line enclosing a separate inset of Amboy Avenue, which forms its own part, and the right edge shows lots of the adjoining sheet. A compass rose stands in the open land at the right.
notes: Laurence is Lawrence Street in OpenStreetMap; Cedar is West Cedar Street and East Cedar Street.

Walnut Avenue, Myrtle Avenue, Orchard Avenue and Maple Avenue are not used as control: the modern Main Street line lies 20 to 35 m east of the drawn Main south of Charles, so their junctions with Main are displaced.

Control rests on the Charles / George, Charles / Lawrence and George / Lincoln Avenue junctions and a hand-picked Main / Brunswick Avenue point; the lower half of the sheet has no control of its own and is extrapolated.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main map (Main, Lincoln Av, George, Charles, Laurence, Walnut Av, Myrtle Av, Orchard Av, Maple Av, Cedar; cemetery), control from three junctions in the upper third and Main / Brunswick, plus points carried from sheet 18 where added (low confidence); 2 inset lower right (heavy line) of Amboy Av at Green, Howland Pl, Linsley Pl, Coan Pl, anchored on Amboy / Linsley (low confidence).

sheet-19-2.description: An inset at the lower right of the sheet, at 100 feet to an inch, bounded on the north and west by a heavy line and showing a separate piece of the south-eastern part of Metuchen along the Raritan Township line. Amboy Avenue crosses the top of the inset from the corner of the heavy line to the right edge, with a group of dwellings on lots of block 197 at the left and block 198 in the centre. Green runs south from Amboy Avenue and is lettered not open. Linsley Place and Coan Place run south from Amboy Avenue at the right, and Howland Place crosses the lots between Green and Linsley Place. The blocks at the right edge, numbered 199 and 17, are drawn as narrow lots with no buildings. The borough line with Raritan Township crosses the upper right corner on a diagonal. A railroad (L.V.R.R.) runs diagonally through the lower half of the inset. A cemetery lies at the bottom and an arrow marks north inside the inset; its direction disagrees with the streets, so the street directions were used instead. The inset has no street junction with any other part of the sheet and is placed from a single junction, so its position is uncertain.
notes: Green is lettered not open; Howland Place is not in the OpenStreetMap extract.

The Amboy Avenue / Green Street and Amboy Avenue / Coan Place junctions of the modern data did not agree with the drawn spacing (the three junctions fit at a scale 7 percent too small), so only Amboy Avenue / Linsley Place was used, with the scale and direction taken from the sheet.
The inset was placed from one hand-picked point plus a scale of 3.94 px/ft and a north direction of 1.4 degrees worked out from the bearing of Amboy Avenue; it is low confidence.
